label: rem:axiom-independence
title: Independence of the QU axioms
html:
Remark. Independence of the QU axioms

Are the four axioms of a quantum universe independent?

Temporal braiding. Over a characteristic-zero field, Deligne's theorem shows every symmetric monoidal category admits a fibre functor. We require only a braiding, and only over a commutative ring, so the fibre functor is not supplied for us. The braiding axiom is independent of the fibre functor.

Frobenius--Hopf. A general Hopf algebra need not carry a non-degenerate Frobenius form. The Frobenius condition A \cong A^{\vee} is strictly stronger than the Hopf axioms.

Symmetric Frobenius. A Frobenius algebra need not be symmetric: the left and right traces induced by a non-symmetric form differ by the Nakayama automorphism, which is trivial exactly when the form is symmetric. The axiom is therefore a genuine restriction on the Frobenius--Hopf datum, not a consequence of it.

Wedderburn semisimplicity. A Frobenius object need not be semisimple: a truncated polynomial algebra k[x]/(x^n) carries a non-degenerate Frobenius form and is local, hence has a single block and a nilpotent radical. Semisimplicity is therefore independent of the preceding three axioms. It is the assumption that does the work later: given it, the co-Casimir trace identity (Frobenius co-Casimir universal) follows by linearity over the central idempotents rather than being assumed.

The differential calculus \Omega^1(A) is a separate matter. For smooth algebraic groups Kähler differentials exist automatically, but for quantum groups (q \neq 1) a differential calculus need not exist or be unique, so its existence is an assumption rather than a theorem.

In full generality, all four axioms are independent.
